reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in constructing a reproducible pipeline from raw play-by-play data to player-level performance metrics. The expected points model uses multinomial logistic regression to predict scoring outcomes conditioned on game state variables such as down, distance, and field position. This provides a foundational scalar measure of play value. Win probability estimation extends this by incorporating temporal and score-based dynamics via generalized additive models, offering a continuous-time view of game influence. Finally, the nflWAR framework applies multilevel modeling to decompose total team success into individual contributions, isolating each player’s marginal impact on win probability. Each primitive builds upon prior ones: EPA informs WP, which in turn supports WAR estimation. The resampling approach ensures robustness against data variability and selection bias. Dualities emerge between deterministic play evaluation and stochastic outcome modeling, while failure modes occur at data sparsity or model misalignment with evolving game strategies.
